title: Waveform rollout scribe and rollback safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a policy engine and configuration authoring flow for waveform-style canary rollouts. We need a compact DSL + runtime enforcement that expresses arbitrary step schedules (percentages, durations, mirror/shadow stages), traffic split composition (nested A/B + canary), guardrails (metric thresholds, growth limits), and automated rollback semantics. This ticket covers the core schema, enforcement primitives in the router, and integration hooks with Console telemetry and Alerts to drive automated rollback and manual intervention flows. Goal: ship a minimal safe default that supports progressive exposure to 1%, 10%, 50% waves, plus optional shadow probing and concurrent A/B arms, with deterministic rollback behavior and audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: Config schema (DSL) approved by PM and Design
Runtime can parse and validate DSL and reject invalid configs
Router enforces step schedule and applies traffic splits deterministically
Guardrails evaluate metric windows and trigger rollback actions within SLA budget
Console surfaces per-step telemetry and an action button to abort/advance rollout
End-to-end test harness simulates degradations and verifies automated rollback
decisions: Use a declarative YAML-first DSL for rollout definitions with JSON storage in config service
Enforce guardrail evaluation at the routing layer with guaranteed-at-most-once enforcement of rollback actions
Expose a compact SDK for programmatic rollouts (Node/Python) that maps to the same DSL
Opt for percentile-based latency and request-error-rate as primary guardrail signals; allow custom metrics via labels
implementation_notes: Phase 1: schema + validator + simple runtime that supports sequential percent waves and shadow probing
Phase 2: add nested A/B arms, canary bundling, and inhibition timers between steps
Router change: add token-aware splitper that consults rollout controller for current step allocation
Rollback: router issues a single rollback mutation to config service; controller ensures idempotent application and writes an audit entry
Telemetry: emit per-step events (step_entered, step_exited, guardrail_violation, rollback_triggered) to ampel/metrics-stream
config_schema_example:
rollout_name: waveform-experiment-2026
strategy:
  type: waveform
  steps:
    - id: step-1
      percent: 1
      duration: 10m
      probes:
        - name: latency-p95
          metric: latency.p95
          comparator: lt
          threshold_ms: 250
    - id: step-2
      percent: 10
      duration: 30m
    - id: step-3
      percent: 50
      duration: 60m
  shadow:
    enabled: true
    sample_rate: 0.05
guardrails:
  - name: request_error_rate
    metric: requests.error_rate
    window: 5m
    threshold: 0.02
    action: rollback
  - name: latency_regression
    metric: latency.p95
    window: 10m
    delta_pct: 20
    action: halt
automations:
  auto_rollback: true
  rollback_cooldown: 15m
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial scoping doc added. Marked risk areas: metric noise for multi-tenant workloads and race conditions when two rollouts target the same model. Suggest adding per-rollout lease to avoid conflicting mutations.

2026-03-04 - Miguel Torres: Proof-of-concept router splitper merged to feature branch. Observed ~3% extra CPU on 1000tps when evaluating guardrails inline; we'll prototype an offloaded aggregator to compute windows asynchronously.
2026-03-06 - Priya Sharma (PM): Reviewed DSL; please make 'action' enum explicit (rollback|halt|notify) and add 'sensitivity' tag for noisy metrics so Console can surface confidence levels.
2026-03-08 - Security review note from Lucas Nguyen: Shadow traffic must be opt-in per-org and respect PII routing policy. KMS key access audit required in Private deployments.
2026-03-10 - Miguel Torres: Implemented validator + unit tests for DSL. Next: integrate with rollout controller and add e2e harness to simulate degraded variants.
tests: Unit: schema validation rejects missing 'steps' and invalid percent sums (>100)
Integration: router applies step allocations after controller transitions (simulated time)
Chaos: inject 30% request error rate into canary variant and assert auto-rollback occurs within configured window
Load: 10k tps synthetic traffic with rollouts enabled; verify throughput and CPU overhead under 5% relative to baseline
